title: Rumor: Kendrick Lamar to Feature on New Clipse Album
htmlContent:
Hip-hop fans are excited about a potential Kendrick Lamar appearance on Clipse's upcoming album, 'Let God Sort Em Out.' This speculation has ignited the internet, leaving fans eager for confirmation from the artists themselves.

The Source of the Rumor

A TikTok video was the source of the rumor, which was unexpected. Creator Nigel Cooper, known for his hip-hop content, accidentally sparked speculation while discussing the 2023 feud between Pusha T and Jim Jones. Cooper's video incorporated snippets of various tracks, including the unreleased Clipse song 'Chains & Whips', which caused eyebrows to rise in the hip-hop community. According to Cooper, TikTok muted the audio in his video after receiving a copyright strike from Universal Music Group (UMG). What is intriguing? The copyright claim allegedly mentions Kendrick Lamar as a featured artist on 'Chains & Whips.'

A History of Collaboration

Kendrick has previously worked with Pusha T, but this is his first time working with Clipse as a duo. The two artists collaborated on 'Nosetalgia,' a standout track from Pusha's 2013 solo debut, 'My Name Is My Name.'

The Album's Progress

For months, Pusha T has joked with his fans about the new Clipse album. In a recent appearance on the Ghetto Runways podcast, he revealed that the album is finished, with just one feature remaining. Is Kendrick Lamar the actual name of this mysterious feature? At Miami Art Week, Pusha revealed more information about the project: "It's been 15 years since we dropped an album. We've been at it since '98/'99 but I think people are gonna witness greatness [...] You will get to see how street Hip Hop matures."

What to Expect

The hip-hop world is anticipating the release of 'Let God Sort Em Out' as a significant release. The album, produced entirely by Pharrell Williams, is a reunion of longtime collaborators and friends. Pusha T emphasized their meticulous approach to the music, implying that fans can expect nothing short of excellence. Expectations are high for Clipse's first album since 2009's 'Til the Casket Drops' and their debut release on Def Jam. Whether or not Kendrick Lamar makes an appearance, one thing is sure: hip-hop enthusiasts are in for a treat when 'Let God Sort Em Out' finally drops. Keep an eye out for official announcements from Clipse and Kendrick Lamar about these exciting rumors. Until then, fans can revisit classic Clipse tracks and ponder the potential of this star-studded collaboration.
